modules.name: 授权与知识读取权限执行
modules.scope: 应用自定义 HTTP 端点如何用 @nocobase/authorization 的资源/动作判定与数据库策略执行“谁可读已发布知识、谁可改”，覆盖 B05、B01、B04。
modules.limitations: 未逐一审计所有自定义端点是否都执行了资源动作判定；本模块聚焦 B05 涉及的知识读取路径。

requirements.need: 没有阅读动作权限的账号（含无业务权限的集成账号）不能仅因文章已发布就读取正文。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供资源类型/动作判定、记录访问与数据库策略；应用在自定义端点对动作做 authorize 并用 withPolicy 约束读取。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 自定义端点安装 authz.middleware()，调用 c.var.authz.authorize({resource, action})，拒绝缺失表策略并以 repository.withPolicy() 读取（repository-routes.md 第21行）。
requirements.actualUsage: service-content.ts 的 GET /service/knowledge 只做 requireActor + isSupervisor，并按 published 过滤；未调用 authorize/withPolicy，导致 qanobody 与 svc.integration 均可读已发布正文。

requirements.need: 未登录者不能读取或写入业务数据。
requirements.responsibility: 认证插件与授权中间件在路由入口拒绝匿名访问。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 路由挂 authentication.required() 与 authz.middleware()。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用路由统一使用 requireActor；B01 的正反用例通过。

requirementFit.reason: 授权模型（资源类型+动作+记录访问+数据库策略）直接覆盖“按动作授权读取”的需求，B05 的失败源于应用端点未执行该判定，而非框架缺能力。

usability.reason: middleware + context.require + withPolicy 的用法在库与 Skill 中有一致的完整示例，接入路径清晰。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 用决策表区分生成式路由与自定义端点，并给出明确“必须 authorize/withPolicy”的规则。

design.reason: 判定、资源注册、记录访问与持久化解耦，library 不含存储、由应用插件提供数据库适配，职责边界清楚。

reliability.reason: 中间件在请求级建立上下文并串行执行，拒绝语义统一为 403 AUTHORIZATION_DENIED；实现对未注册类型/条件判定采取拒绝默认。

modules.name: 调度器的受控触发与启停
modules.scope: 主管在页面受控触发一次巡检/超期提醒生成，以及计划的启用/停用与 occurrence 记录，覆盖 B08。
modules.limitations: 未在真实定时边界（跨天、时区切换）复现计划触发；结论基于归档的 B08 证据与实现阅读。

requirements.need: 主管能在 UI 上“立即触发一次”某计划，使生成动作走受控 Scheduler 并写入 occurrence。
requirements.responsibility: 插件拥有调度与触发；应用只声明定义和业务目标。
requirements.recommendedUsage: Skill 只提供 defineSchedule/registerTarget 与 list/enable/disable/occurrences 管理面；operations.md 明确执行器/channel 对插件私有、不可从容器解析。
requirements.actualUsage: runScheduleNow 直接查 schedule_definitions 表、解析 jobExecutorServiceToken 取得 schedule executor、访问私有 runner 字段并手工 recordEvent，绕过 Skill 明示的私有边界。

requirements.need: 计划启用/停用保存正确，停用后不再产生新的受控结果。
requirements.responsibility: 插件持久化计划状态并在 dispatch 时遵循 enabled。
requirements.actualUsage: B08 通过：停用后 Next trigger 变 —，受控触发不再生成新任务。

requirementFit.reason: 计划定义/启停与 occurrence 记录可靠，但“立即执行一次”这一常见管理需求没有公开 API，只能靠访问私有 runner 与查私有表实现。

usability.reason: 缺少受控触发端点或服务方法；文档又明确禁止访问执行器/私有表，使应用陷入“要么违规要么无法实现”的选择。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 把私有边界写得很清楚，但没有给出替代的受控触发方案或示例，Agent 只能自行猜测私有字段。

design.reason: 执行器与 occurrence 存储的私有化有利于封装，但把“管理员手动触发”一并排除，导致能力与公开面不匹配。

reliability.reason: 启停、带时区计划、occurrence 对账与重复触发去重按文档真实工作；但应用绕行依赖私有 runner 字段，升级后会静默失效。

modules.name: 源码管理工作流的上线激活
modules.scope: 应用随构建携带 workflow 源码 Artifact 时，如何在不依赖人工管理操作的前提下将其置为可执行，覆盖 B02（及依赖工单流程的 B03/B07）。
modules.limitations: 未验证多实例并发启用或版本回滚场景；结论基于归档 B02/B03 结果与源码阅读。

requirements.need: 应用安装/升级后自带的工作流无需人工点“启用新版本”即可运行，且能识别新 Artifact 版本而非静默跑旧版。
requirements.responsibility: 插件拥有 Artifact 生命周期、revision 与启用状态；应用只负责提供源码并经公开 API 激活。
requirements.recommendedUsage: Skill 仅说明 trigger() 与“构建/同步/启用/调用是独立阶段”；启用走 worklfow 管理 API POST /api/workflows/<hash>/enable。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用 Provider 断言 workflowServiceToken 为私有运行时接口，调用 discoverArtifacts/ensureArtifactMaterialized，再直接 updateMany/updateOne workflows 表把 revision 置 current+enabled。

requirements.need: 业务触发已发布工作流并取得持久运行记录。
requirements.responsibility: 插件提供 trigger 与运行持久化。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 解析 workflowServiceToken 调 trigger(key, input)，按 event key 查询运行。
requirements.actualUsage: B02 通过，运行记录与分支结果一致，重复受理不重复执行。

requirementFit.reason: 运行与持久化直接可用，但“随应用上线同一版本无需人工启用”的整条路径没有公开 API，只能访问包内方法并直写状态表。

usability.reason: 公开契约仅 trigger/registerInstruction；启用状态只能经管理 API 或数据库，源码托管应用缺少可信的编程入口。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 正确说明各阶段分离，但未给出源码应用自激活的受支持方式，Agent 必须逆推 internal token 与表结构。

design.reason: Artifact/revision/执行状态模型清晰，但把“激活”排除在公开服务之外，与应用“安装即可用”的诉求冲突。

reliability.reason: trigger 对 disabled/not-found/重复事件的处理明确且持久化真实，B02/B03 流程行为由运行记录支撑；绕行部分依赖非公开字段，稳定性无保证。

modules.scope: 业务表单提交日期与时间值、以及 createdAt/updatedAt 的维护责任，涉及 @nocobase/db 的 Collection Builder 与 Repository 校验。
modules.limitations: 未覆盖 time/datetimeTz 与时区边界的运行验证；结论来自实现对与归档证据。

requirements.need: 浏览器日期控件提交的 date-only 或 datetime-local 值能按用户看到的时刻落库。
requirements.responsibility: 框架拥有类型定义与校验；应用选择字段类型并把控件值规范到框架接受的形状。
requirements.recommendedUsage: Skill 列出 date/datetime 字段与 Repository 写入，但未提示两种形状差异及框架只接受完整 V1 值。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用另写 normalizeDateTime 补齐秒/毫秒后写入，说明框架校验与表单控件之间需要应用层桥接。

requirements.need: 记录写入后 createdAt/updatedAt 可用且可排序。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供字段类型与写入校验；未自动维护时需明确由应用负责。
requirements.recommendedUsage: Skill 的迁移示例声明 createdAt，却未说明写入时谁负责填充。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用自写 stamped/createdAtStamp/touched 在每个写点手工填两个时间字段。

requirementFit.reason: date/datetime 类型与严格校验能满足需求，但表单常见形状与框架契约不一致，需要应用额外规范化。

usability.reason: 严格 V1 校验减少脏数据，但对 date-only/datetime-local 没有内建容错或提示；createdAt/updatedAt 无自动或辅助写入。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 未点明两条易踩的写入语义，Agent 只能通过报错反推并自建工具函数。

design.reason: 时间类型建模与失败原因（INVALID_MUTATION + 字段路径）清晰，校验与存储分离合理。

reliability.reason: 校验拒绝无效日历值与错误偏移，读取时对存储值做对称归一，行为一致可测。

requirements.need: 工单详情等子页面在不产生双重前缀的情况下可达，导航分组与子路由路径一致。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供路由树解析与冲突检测；应用按相对/绝对规则声明 path。
requirements.recommendedUsage: Skill 说明无 path 的分组内页面使用完整路径，子路由相对父路由声明。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用修复为“分组不声明 path + 子页面完整路径 + 详情相对 :ticketId”，并加注释解释原双重前缀错误。

requirementFit.reason: 路由解析支持完整路径与相对子路由两种写法，可满足业务页面与详情页需求。

usability.reason: 规则可用但以“拼接”实现：分组带 path 且子项以 / 开头时会静默产生 /a/a/b，没有可读的校验错误。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 用示例讲清两种写法，但未强调以 / 开头的子路径仍会被拼到父路径这一反直觉行为。

design.reason: 路由解析、导航与权限声明分离，冲突检测覆盖重复 path；拼接语义可预测但缺少边界提示。

reliability.reason: 解析对缺 path、无效 path、重复注册均给出明确错误；对双重前缀这一合法但易错的组合不报错。

findings.title: 授权库提供从资源动作判定到数据库策略的完整自定义端点接入路径
findings.detail: authorization 库以资源类型+动作+recordAccess 判定，并通过 authz.middleware()/context.require() 在请求级执行；应用插件补齐数据库策略；Skill 用决策表明确自定义端点必须 authorize 并 withPolicy。
findings.impact: 应用能把“谁可读已发布知识”表达为可复用、可测试的授权模型，而不是散落的路由内 if。
findings.suggestedChange: 保持该分层与示例；可再补一个“自定义读取端点拒绝无动作权限”的负例测试模板。

findings.title: GET /service/knowledge 未执行资源动作判定，已发布内容对无权限账号可读
findings.detail: service-content.ts 的知识读取只做 requireActor + isSupervisor + published 过滤，未调用 authz.authorize/withPolicy；而 service-authorization.ts 已声明 knowledgePublished 与 service.knowledge 授权。
findings.impact: B05 失败：普通 Member（qanobody）与无业务权限的集成账号（svc.integration）都能读取已发布知识全文，越过了“无阅读动作权限不得因已发布而访问”的要求。
findings.suggestedChange: 在该端点安装 authz.middleware()，先 authorize(service.knowledge/read) 并对返回的 database 策略用 repository.withPolicy() 读取，草稿可见性由 supervisor 动作单独授权。

diagnosis.trigger: 无阅读动作权限的账号请求 GET /service/knowledge。
diagnosis.expected: 按资源动作判定拒绝，或仅返回被授予的记录。
diagnosis.actual: 任何已认证账号都能读取所有 published 文章正文。
diagnosis.workaround: 应用已在授权声明中定义 knowledgePublished/页面动作，可立即在路由执行。
diagnosis.acceptance: qanobody 与 svc.integration 请求该端点被拒；有阅读动作权限的工程师只能读到其范围内的已发布文章。

findings.title: Scheduler 无公开“立即执行一次”能力，应用只能访问私有 runner 与私有表
findings.detail: 公开 SchedulerService 仅 registerTarget/defineSchedule，HTTP 仅 list/get/enable/disable/occurrences；operations.md 又明确 store、target registry、schedule executor 对插件私有、应用不得解析。应用 runScheduleNow 因此直接查 schedule_definitions 并访问 executor.runner 私有字段。
findings.impact: 管理员“现在生成一次”这类常见需求没有受支持入口；应用的绕行依赖私有字段与私有表，插件升级后会静默失效或抛错。
findings.suggestedChange: 提供一个受授权保护的“run now/manual trigger”服务方法或 HTTP 端点（记录 occurrence、遵守 enabled），或明确给出受支持的从应用触发单个计划 firing 的 API。

diagnosis.trigger: 主管在仪表盘点击 Generate 要求立即执行一次计划。
diagnosis.expected: 经公开服务或受授权端点触发一次 firing 并写入 occurrence。
diagnosis.actual: 只能查私有 schedule_definitions、访问私有 executor.runner 并手工 recordEvent。
diagnosis.workaround: 应用直接读私有表/私有字段并复用 recordEvent，当前可用但违反文档边界。
diagnosis.acceptance: 存在受支持的触发入口，不再依赖私有表与私有 runner，且 occurrence/重复执行语义与定时触发一致。

feedbackReview.reason: 证据链一致：Scheduler 公开服务仅 registerTarget/defineSchedule，HTTP 只有 list/get/occurrences/enable/disable，插件 Skill 明确 store、target registry、schedule executor 私有；应用 runScheduleNow 直接查 schedule_definitions 并访问私有 executor.runner、手工 recordEvent，确无受支持的“按计划立即执行一次”入口。Skill 提供的 JobExecutor 面向不需要 UI 可观测的一过性异步任务，不产生计划的 occurrence，也不能替代“主管触发 UI 可见计划并记录 occurrence”的需求。

checks.reason: E65 公开服务只有 registerTarget 与 defineSchedule 两个扩展点；E66 的管理路由只有 list/get/occurrences/enable/disable；E68 明确 store、target registry、schedule executor 对插件私有、应用不得从容器解析。契约层面没有触发单个计划 firing 的受支持入口。
E79 显示 runScheduleNow 读 schedule_definitions 取 nextRunAt、按 scheduler.jobs 解析 jobExecutorServiceToken 取得 executor、访问私有 runner 字段并手工 recordEvent(Start/End)，即实际只能绕行；E66 证明公开 HTTP 面无对应端点可调用。
应用直读私有计划表并访问私有 runner，确实违反 E68 记录的文档边界；但所需能力在公开面上不存在，绕行是当时唯一可行路径，因此这是插件缺口而非单纯应用误用。候选也如实标注了“当前可用但违反文档边界”。
没有外部服务、凭据或运行环境因素更能解释现象；E86 显示 Scheduler Skill 对“立即异步执行”的建议是 JobExecutor，但它针对无需 UI 跟踪的任务且不写计划 occurrence，与主管触发已登记计划的需求不等价，故不能据此否定缺口。
现有指引来自插件自身 Skill(E68)，未见工厂提示、注入配置或模板要求应用直写 schedule_definitions；缺相应工厂材料，故不把成因归于工厂。
现成公开入口只有 enable/disable 与 occurrences 查询(E65,E66)，scheduler sync 不触发 firing(E68)，JobExecutor(E86) 不满足 occurrence 语义。没有现有公开入口能满足“立即执行一次并写入 occurrence”，改进空间成立。

findings.title: Workflow 公开契约不含激活/启用，源码托管应用须访问包内方法并直写状态表
findings.detail: workflowServiceToken 仅暴露 registerInstruction/trigger；Artifact 物化与 revision 启用不在公开契约中。应用的 Provider 断言 token 为私有运行时接口、调用 discoverArtifacts/ensureArtifactMaterialized，再直接 updateMany/updateOne workflows 表。
findings.impact: 随应用发布的源码工作流无法经公开 API 在安装后自动启用，必须触碰内部方法与表结构；升级后易碎。
findings.suggestedChange: 在公开服务中提供“按 Artifact hash 物化并激活/启用 revision”的受权方法（或在文档中给出受支持的编程启用方式）。

diagnosis.trigger: 应用带自有 workflow 源码启动，需要其版本立即可运行。
diagnosis.expected: 公开 API 物化并启用正确 revision。
diagnosis.actual: 调用非公开的 ensureArtifactMaterialized 并直写 workflows.current/enabled。
diagnosis.workaround: 应用 Provider 自行物化、清理旧 current、置新 revision current+enabled，幂等但有竞态与升级风险。
diagnosis.acceptance: 公开入口可完成“构建→同步→启用”，应用不再引用内部方法或直写状态表。

feedbackReview.reason: E69/E70 只证明服务 token 的契约不含激活；但 E72 与官方 reference E85 明确记载受权管理 API，E87 的 POST /workflows/:workflowId/enable 说明按 hash 可物化并置为 current 且 enabled。源码工作流有受支持的公开 HTTP 入口完成“物化→启用”，E72 还明示应用应使用公开 API、不得绕过内部方法与物化表。因此“无法经公开 API 启用、必须触碰内部方法”这一具体结论被反证；应用使用私有方法属违反既有指引，而非插件能力缺口。

checks.reason: E69 的 WorkflowServiceContract 仅含 registerInstruction/trigger；E70 的类上有 discoverArtifacts/ensureArtifactMaterialized 但不在契约。这支持“服务 token 未导出激活方法”这一狭窄事实，但不足以支持“公开面没有启用能力”。
E77 应用把 workflowServiceToken 断言为私有运行时接口，调用 discoverArtifacts/ensureArtifactMaterialized，并 updateMany/updateOne workflows 表置 current/enabled。行为本身属实，但在存在公开管理 API 的情况下只证明应用选择了绕行，不证明公开面缺失。
E72 要求业务/应用使用公开 API 并明确不得绕过插件内部或直接编辑物化表；E85 记录管理方法 enable(idOrArtifactHash) 及“这些不是包根服务导出”。应用绕过受权管理 API 直写 workflows 表，属误用/未满足前提。
不存在缺少外部环境材料的问题：受权管理 API 在部署后可调用(E87)，E85 说明 enable 支持物化未同步的 Artifact，无需依赖包内服务导出。环境因素不能解释为缺口。
未见工厂提示、注入配置或模板要求应用直写 workflow 表；现有边界来自插件 Skill(E72)，不归因工厂。
已有公开入口 E87(POST /workflows/:workflowId/enable，按 hash 物化并启用) 与 E85(enable(idOrArtifactHash))，并由 E72 指引用于启用；即“构建→同步→启用”的受支持公开路径已存在。候选所称的公开能力缺失不成立。

findings.title: nocobase-db Skill 未说明 datetime 输入形状与 createdAt/updatedAt 的写入责任
findings.detail: Repository 只接受完整 V1 时间值，而浏览器 date/datetime-local 提交部分值；Skill 的迁移示例声明 createdAt 却不说明写入时由谁填充。应用因此自写 normalizeDateTime 与 stamped/touched。
findings.impact: Agent 需要从 INVALID_MUTATION 报错反推契约并反复自建工具函数，增加试错与被拒写入。
findings.suggestedChange: 在 nocobase-db 中补充：datetime 字段接受的完整形状与常见控件值的桥接方式，以及 createdAt/updatedAt 是否自动维护、若不自动由谁负责。

diagnosis.trigger: 用 date/datetime-local 值写 datetime 字段，或插入未填 createdAt 的记录。
diagnosis.expected: Skill 事先说明可接受形状与字段维护责任。
diagnosis.actual: 只能靠报错/源码判断，应用自建 normalize 与 timestamp 辅助。
diagnosis.workaround: 应用自写 normalizeDateTime 与时间戳辅助函数。
diagnosis.acceptance: Skill 明确记录两条写入语义，后续应用无需重复试错。

feedbackReview.reason: E73 证明 datetime 只接受完整 V1（含秒）值，date-only 与 datetime-local 的部分值会被拒；E74 的 db Skill 迁移示例只声明 createdAt 为 not null，未说明写入时谁填充，全文最接近的表述仅是 E88“Repository 负责时序编码”，也未给出可接受输入形状或 createdAt/updatedAt 责任。应用因此自写 normalizeDateTime(E80) 与 stamped/touched(E81)。属可依据源码与指引证实的文档改进空间。

checks.reason: E73 的 Repository 契约要求合法 V1 temporal 值（含秒，毫秒以内），部分值直接 INVALID_MUTATION；E74 的示例把 createdAt 声明为 not null 却不给默认值或填充约定。
E80 应用补齐 date 与 datetime-local 的部分值以适配严格校验；E81 手工写 createdAt/updatedAt 并注明框架不自动填充。两者对应契约未说明的两处写入语义。
应用自建桥接与时间戳辅助并非错误装配：E80 的注释说明保留 collection 校验为唯一权威，E81 的辅助保证业务写入不漏字段。它们反映的是 Skill 未覆盖该语义。
无外部服务或运行环境因素更优解释；db 包内未见自动填充 createdAt/updatedAt 的逻辑(E81)，Skill 中唯一相关表述是 E88 的时序编码职责。
没有工厂提示、注入配置或模板材料涉及该写入语义；现有材料是 db Skill 示例(E74)，故不归因工厂。
现有 Skill 对 temporal 的最接近覆盖是 E88“Repository 负责时序编码”，并未给出可接受形状或 createdAt/updatedAt 责任；E73 与 E74 共同说明缺口，补充指引的改进空间成立。

findings.title: 客户端路由对“分组带 path + 子项以 / 开头”静默双重前缀，无提示
findings.detail: plugins.js 将子路由 normalize 后直接拼到父路径；当分组声明 path 且子项用 /service/... 时得到 /service/service/...，最终页面不可达且无明确错误。
findings.impact: 开发期只表现为页面 404/重复注册，排查成本高（应用确实先出现该问题，后经注释与调整才修复）。
findings.suggestedChange: 当父分组有 path 且子项 path 以 / 开头时给出可读的构建期告警或错误，或在文档中显著标注该语义。

diagnosis.trigger: 导航分组声明 path，子项用 /a/b 形式。
diagnosis.expected: 构建时提示相对/绝对语义冲突。
diagnosis.actual: 静默拼接为 /parent/a/b，页面不可达。
diagnosis.workaround: 应用改为分组不声明 path，子项使用完整路径。
diagnosis.acceptance: 冲突组合在构建期得到明确提示，或不再产生双重前缀。

feedbackReview.reason: E75 显示父路径与子路径直接拼接：子路径先去前导斜杠再前置 /，随后 parentPath + relative，故分组 path='/service' 加子项 '/service/tickets' 得 '/service/service/tickets'；E76 说明只有不声明 path 的分组内页面才用完整路径；E82 记录应用先出现该重复前缀并改为分组不声明 path。E89 显示仅在路径已注册冲突时抛错，不针对该声明组合告警，属可证实的可用性改进点。

checks.reason: E76 规定无 path 的导航分组内页面使用完整路径、子路由相对父路由声明；E75 是其实现，且不会把以 / 开头的子路径视为应用绝对路径。
E75 的拼接逻辑对分组 path + 绝对子路径产生双重前缀；E82 的应用注释确认该组合曾注册 /service/service/... 并使页面重复/不可达，随后修复。
应用最初声明分组 path 并使用 /service/... 子路径，正好触发该组合；改为分组无 path、子项用完整路径后恢复，属应用侧真实触发路径而非环境问题。
无外部服务、凭据或运行时因素参与；路径结果完全由解析规则与声明组合决定(E75)。
未见工厂提示、注入配置或模板要求该声明组合；成因在客户端路由解析规则，不归因工厂。
E89 只在路径已注册冲突时抛错，未对“父有 path + 子绝对路径”给出可读告警；E75 的 normalizeRoutePath 也只校验绝对路径格式。现有能力不含该提示，构建期告警的改进空间成立。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Built the equipment after-sales service & inspection system directly into the NocoBase 3 application (no per-feature publish plugin). Added five migrations and an idempotent seed for customers/devices/tickets/inspections/knowledge/shares/attachments/acceptance logs/reminders/manuals/assistant messages; four job permission sets with page and record scopes; a TicketService with the full 待受理→待处理→处理中→待确认→已关闭 lifecycle, workflow-triggered acceptance with retryable failure records, temporary ticket sharing, repair attachments (PNG + DOCX) behind a private read guard, in-app messages, Scheduler-driven daily inspection generation and overdue reminders, dashboard counters, an API-key device-platform interface with event-number idempotency, a manual-to-knowledge-base sync and a grounded service assistant with citations and a resolution-note draft. Added the /service client pages, routes, navigation and zh/en locales. Rewired the source-managed ticket-acceptance workflow to share the ticket service across the materialized artifact copy, and added a provider that activates the current workflow revision on boot. Self-tests: full vitest suite 42 files / 257 tests pass (including a 12-case service lifecycle/permission/integration test booted from a real install), plus scoped prettier, eslint, all three tsc projects, the workflow check, the collections --check and a full production build. Repair round 3 fixed two verified failures: the on-demand Operations run now executes through the same Scheduler schedule target and occurrence records the timed firing uses (server/service/schedule-runner.ts; runCount, lastRunAt and nextRunAt preserved; failures recorded as ScheduleError; unique per click; direct-call fallback kept when Scheduler is absent), and the assistant draft workflow now has explicit 建议进入草稿/取消/确认保存 controls on both the standalone page and the ticket detail, backed by a persisted, confirmed ticket draft that never changes the status or closes the ticket (migration 202610010006_add_ticket_assistant_draft.ts, TicketService.saveAssistantDraft, POST /service/tickets/:id/assistant-draft). Added regression tests for both; scoped typecheck, eslint, prettier and the affected vitest files pass. Repair round 4 fixed one verified failure: the daily inspection generator now skips enabled devices whose nextInspectionAt is after the planned day (server/service/ticket-service.ts, isInspectionDue) instead of generating for every enabled device, and the seed now includes the overdue open/closed tickets the task requires (database/main/seeds/202610010010_service_test_data.ts). Reworked the inspection idempotency test to create a due and a future device, and added a closed-overdue reminder-exclusion test. Scoped server tsc, eslint and prettier pass; tests/logic/service-equipment.test.ts 26 tests pass. Repair round 5 fixed the reported device-save failure: a browser date control submits a partial temporal value (`YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` for datetime-local) that the `datetime` collection validator refuses with 400 INVALID_MUTATION. Added server/service/scalars.ts normalizeDateTime and applied it to devices.nextInspectionAt (route create + patch) and tickets.dueAt (TicketService.createTicket), so a next inspection date can be set, updated, cleared, and the device disabled/reassigned from the UI again. Regression test covers date-only device create/patch and a minute-precision dueAt ticket; server tsc, scoped eslint and the 27-test service-equipment file pass.

blockers.title: Workflow run modules cannot import application server code
blockers.symptom: The ticket-acceptance workflow failed at runtime with `Run module "../../../server/service/ticket-service.js" resolves outside its artifact`, and a temporary test showed `Cannot find module '/tmp/.../storage/workflows/server/service/ticket-service.js'`.
blockers.rootCause: A workflow artifact is materialized into a content-addressed copy under storage/workflows/<key>/<digest>/ and the loader enforces containment, and bare package imports are not reliably resolvable from that copy, so handler modules must be self-contained. The app registered its service under a token created by createServiceToken('...'), whose value is a fresh object, so even a handler that described the same token name would hold a different Map key.
blockers.resolution: Added workflows/ticket-acceptance/server/tokens.ts which derives the token from a process-global Symbol.for('equipment-service/service.ticket'), and changed server/service/ticket-service.ts to use the same Symbol.for literal. The app container and the artifact copy now resolve one service. Handlers keep type-only imports for their flow context and use a structural port instead of importing the service class.

blockers.title: NocoBase 3 does not manage createdAt/updatedAt
blockers.symptom: Writing tickets failed with `NOT NULL constraint failed: tickets.created_at`.
blockers.rootCause: The migration declares createdAt/updatedAt NOT NULL with no database default, and the framework does not stamp them on raw repository writes.
blockers.resolution: Every application create/update goes through server/service/timestamps.ts, which returns the values spread into the record as ISO strings (datetime fields are typed string, so a Date fails type checking too).

blockers.title: A materialized workflow revision is disabled and not current
blockers.symptom: Acceptance returned `{status:'skipped', reason:'not-found'}` / `'disabled'` and the ticket stayed in 待受理 even though the workflow definition was valid.
blockers.rootCause: Workflow materialization creates a workflows row with enabled:false and no current flag; nothing in the application enables it, and there is no CLI command that does.
blockers.resolution: Added server/providers/equipment-workflow-provider.ts, which on every boot materializes the current ticket-acceptance artifact and marks its revision current and enabled. It is idempotent and picks up a new digest after a rebuild.

blockers.title: A seed that imports server/*.js breaks source-installing tests without a TypeScript loader
blockers.symptom: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed with `Cannot find module '/.../server/service-authorization.js' imported from .../database/main/seeds/...ts`.
blockers.rootCause: An installed-from-source boot loads seeds with a native dynamic import. `tsx` remaps a `server/*.js` specifier to the `.ts` source, but the template test did not register it because the template shipped no seed importing server code.
blockers.resolution: Registered the tsx ESM loader in tests/logic/app-server.test.ts (the same way tests/logic/service-equipment.test.ts already did) before the application boots.

blockers.title: Ticket detail page unreachable because a navigation group path was prepended to absolute child paths
blockers.symptom: Clicking a ticket, opening /main/service/tickets/<id> directly, or pushState all redirected to /main; the backend GET /main/api/service/tickets/<id> returned 200, but the client registered /service/service/tickets/service/tickets/:ticketId, so the whole accept/flow/reject/close/share/attachment/draft chain was unusable.
blockers.rootCause: client/routes.ts declared the `service` navigation group with `path: '/service'` AND its children with absolute paths. resolveNode/resolveRouteTree in @nocobase/app-client prepends a group's path to every child, so each absolute child was prefixed a second time. The ticket-detail child was absolute as well and got doubled once more.
blockers.resolution: Removed `path: '/service'` from the service group (kept `auth: 'required'` and navigation) so children carry the full path, and made the ticket-detail child relative (`:ticketId`). `renderRouteTree` handles slicing; the resolved tree now matches /service/tickets and /service/tickets/:ticketId. Commented the reasoning in client/routes.ts and added tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts coverage.

blockers.title: Duplicate device serial surfaced as an opaque server error instead of a described conflict
blockers.symptom: POST /service/devices with an existing serial did not return a clean rejection the UI could explain.
blockers.rootCause: The `devices.serial` uniqueness was enforced only by the database constraint; the raw constraint error surfaced as a 500. Edits had the same problem and no self-exclusion.
blockers.resolution: Added assertSerialAvailable(serial, exceptId?) to server/routes/service-master-data.ts, which looks the serial up first and throws ApiError ALREADY_EXISTS (reason SERVICE_DEVICE_SERIAL_EXISTS, 409). POST calls it for the new serial; PATCH calls it only when the serial changes, passing the device id so keeping its own serial is allowed. Declared 409 on both routes.

blockers.title: Repair ticket creation accepted a device that did not belong to the chosen customer and could be disabled
blockers.symptom: The create form had no Customer field at all (the customer was derived from the device with no way to disagree), and a ticket could be opened against a disabled device.
blockers.rootCause: createTicket() derived customerId from the device and never checked the pair or the device enabled flag, and the client form sent only a device so a mismatch could not even be expressed.
blockers.resolution: createTicket() now resolves customerId = input.customerId ?? device.customerId and rejects a pair mismatch and a disabled device with TicketServiceError('VALIDATION') (400). Validation runs on create only, so historic tickets keep working. The client added an independent Customer Select (not filtered by device, so a mismatch is constructible and rejected) and sends customerId directly; Save requires title, customer and device.

blockers.title: Marking an in-app message read answered 400 Field "updatedAt" does not exist
blockers.symptom: POST /main/api/service/messages/<id>/read returned 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT FIELD_NOT_FOUND '"updatedAt" does not exist'.
blockers.rootCause: markMessageRead used the shared touched() helper, which asks the ORM to write updatedAt, but the service_messages collection has no updatedAt column (it only has read/read_at).
blockers.resolution: markMessageRead now writes { read: true, readAt: new Date().toISOString() } directly, with a comment explaining why touched() is wrong for this collection. Added a regression test that reads an unread message and re-lists it.

blockers.title: A disabled scheduled task still produced inspections through the manual trigger
blockers.symptom: After POST /api/scheduler/schedules/<id>/disable returned 200, the on-demand generate-inspections endpoint still returned {created:1, skipped:8}, so a disabled controlled schedule kept producing new results.
blockers.rootCause: The on-demand trigger called the generation service directly and never consulted the schedule's enabled/lifecycleState state; the scheduler exposes enable/disable over HTTP but no trigger API whose authorization could be reused.
blockers.resolution: Added assertScheduleEnabled(key) to server/routes/service-content.ts: it returns early when the scheduler is not installed, otherwise reads schedule_definitions (app.appName + key) read-only and throws ApiError FAILED_PRECONDITION (400, reason SERVICE_SCHEDULE_DISABLED) when the row is not enabled and active. Wired into both manual operations. No scheduler internals are resolved from the container and the tables are never written.

blockers.title: Dashboard showed no per-engineer workload group
blockers.symptom: The dashboard had total/byStatus/pending counters but no view of how many tickets each engineer held, so the two-engineer split criterion failed.
blockers.rootCause: The dashboard route computed only aggregate counters; no per-owner breakdown existed and zero-ticket engineers could not appear from the ticket rows alone.
blockers.resolution: The dashboard route seeds byEngineer from authorization_permission_set_assignments for service-engineer (so both engineers appear at zero), falls back to the actor for a non-supervisor, counts total/open from the same policy-scoped rows, and sorts by open then total. Added EngineerWorkload to DashboardSummary, a Card in dashboard.tsx, locale strings, and a test asserting both engineers appear.

blockers.title: External ticket lookup by eventNo returned 403 FIELD_READ_FORBIDDEN
blockers.symptom: GET /main/api/service/external/tickets?eventNo=… as the integration account returned 403 FIELD_READ_FORBIDDEN, breaking the platform's primary read path, even though lookup by ticketNo worked.
blockers.rootCause: The service-integration permission set's readable-field list for tickets omitted externalEventNo, and the repository policy stripped/forbade the field the filter used.
blockers.resolution: Added externalEventNo to the service-integration read fields in server/service-authorization.ts (and only that field; customerId stays hidden). The seed re-aligns the permission sets on re-run. Added a test that looks a ticket up by eventNo and reads externalEventNo back.

blockers.title: A supervisor or administrator could not revoke an integration account's API key
blockers.symptom: POST /main/api/auth/api-key/delete {keyId} as admin returned 404 KEY_NOT_FOUND for a key owned by the integration user; only the integration user could manage its own key.
blockers.rootCause: The API Keys plugin page and Better Auth endpoints are self-service, so they only ever act on the caller's own keys, and the plugin's settings page cannot be overridden by an application (route overrides apply to App routes only). No trusted management entry existed.
blockers.resolution: Added server/routes/service-api-keys.ts, registered in server/routes/index.ts: GET /service/integration/api-keys lists keys held by service permission-set holders (read-only apikey + user join) and POST /service/integration/api-keys/:id/revoke calls the plugin's trusted ApiKeyService.remove after ApiKeyService.get. Both are gated by requireSupervisor (service-supervisor or root), and the revoke refuses keys not owned by a service account. Added a supervisor-only card to the Operations page and en/zh locale strings. Added a test that creates a key as the integration user, lists it, revokes it as supervisor, and confirms the key then answers 401.

blockers.title: Operations page crashed after an external ticket submission
blockers.symptom: Submitting an external repair on the Operations page then reading the result crashed the page.
blockers.rootCause: api.request returns the full response body ({ data, meta }) but submitExternal stored the envelope, so the render read fields off `{data}` instead of the ticket.
blockers.resolution: submitExternal (and run()) now unwrap `.data` from api.request before storing/rendering.

blockers.title: Assistant page crashed with TypeError on the answer list
blockers.symptom: Submitting a question on the Assistant page raised a TypeError and the page did not render the answer.
blockers.rootCause: ask() stored the full { data } envelope as the answer, so a later `.map` ran on the envelope rather than the answer object.
blockers.resolution: ask() now destructures `const { data } = await api.request<{ data: AssistantAnswer }>(...)` and sets the answer to `data`.

blockers.title: Assistant citations pointed at routes that do not exist
blockers.symptom: Answer citations linked to paths the App router could not resolve (missing /service prefix).
blockers.rootCause: The assistant route built citation routes from bare page names.
blockers.resolution: service-assistant.ts now emits /service/tickets/<id>, /service/knowledge and /service/manuals citations that match client/routes.ts.

blockers.title: Repeating an acceptance decision ran the acceptance workflow again and duplicated the log and message
blockers.symptom: A second POST /service/tickets/:id/accept for the same pendingAcceptance ticket returned 200 and drove the acceptance workflow to run again, appending another accepted success log and another ticket.assigned in-app message to the engineer; the business requirement is that a repeated status request must not advance state or send a duplicate business message.
blockers.rootCause: requestAcceptance built its workflow eventKey from Date.now(), so every call was a brand-new event and the workflow eventKey dedupe never engaged. The workflow itself also had no ticket-state guard, so even a repeated decision re-applied the update and re-notified.
blockers.resolution: requestAcceptance now reads the ticket first and short-circuits: it answers {status: already-accepted} when decision.accept and ticket.acceptedAt, or {status: already-refused} when !accept and the ticket is closed, without triggering the workflow. The skipped branch uses a stable eventKey (ticket-acceptance:${ticketId}:workflow-skipped). recordStep keeps one row per (eventKey, status) and applyAcceptance is a no-op when the ticket is already past pendingAcceptance, so a genuine retry still runs but a repeat cannot duplicate the log or the assigned message. No separate retry endpoint: the ticket-detail Accept action plus the workflow run record are the recovery path, and a genuine failure keeps a real failed step. Added a test that accepts once, repeats twice, and asserts one accepted:success log, no failed log and one assigned message.

blockers.title: Ticket detail never reflected the accepted priority and the accept form used a stale value
blockers.symptom: After a supervisor accepted a ticket at a chosen priority, the detail page still showed the priority captured when the page first loaded, so a later action submitted the stale value; the acceptance form was also initialized from state that was never re-synced to the loaded ticket.
blockers.rootCause: detail.tsx initialised acceptPriority once from the ticket already in memory and never updated it when the reloaded ticket (or a status transition) changed priority, so React state and the server record diverged.
blockers.resolution: Added a useEffect in detail.tsx keyed on [ticketId, ticketStatus, ticketPriority] that re-syncs acceptPriority from the reloaded ticket, so the accept and edit forms always start from the server value. It deliberately does not set ownerId automatically.

blockers.title: Any signed-in user could read a ticket log, share list and attachments through the observer fallback
blockers.symptom: An engineer who was neither owner, creator, supervisor nor shared reader could open GET /service/tickets/:id and see the full acceptance/handling log, and GET /service/tickets/:id/logs answered 200 with the log message. The detail page rendered the Acceptance card for them.
blockers.rootCause: canViewTicket treated any signed-in user as an observer and returned true, and the detail route pulled logs/shares/attachments straight from an unpolicied repository once the ticket was visible, so the record scope protected only the ticket row, not its internal children.
blockers.resolution: Split the check into canReadTicketInFull (owner, creator, supervisor, or active share) and canViewTicketInternal, and made canViewTicket require the service-observer permission set for the summary-only branch. GET /service/tickets/:id now returns {access: full|summary} and empties logs/shares/attachments for a summary reader; shares are also hidden from an internal non-supervisor. GET .../logs, .../shares and .../attachments require internal (shares additionally supervisor) and answer 403 otherwise. The client gates the log and attachment cards on access==="full". Added a test for an observer seeing access:"summary", empty sections and 403 on all three sub-routes.

blockers.title: Attachment bytes leaked to anyone holding the URL, and a corrupt PNG was accepted as a photo
blockers.symptom: An engineer with no access to the ticket could GET /main/uploads/tickets/<id>.png and receive the bytes, and a 28-byte file named corrupt.png with the wrong content was uploaded and linked as a repair photo with no failure.
blockers.rootCause: canViewFileKey/canViewFileId resolved through the buggy observer fallback, so the /uploads/tickets/* guard allowed any signed-in user, and the file plugin stores any bytes: it enforces only a size limit, so a mislabelled or corrupt file became a ticket attachment.
blockers.resolution: canViewFileKey and canViewFileId now require canViewTicketInternal, so the byte guard follows the same internal-access rule as the ticket. POST /service/tickets/:id/attachments calls TicketService.assertAttachmentContent, which reads the stored bytes through the Drive disk and checks the PNG signature for photo and the ZIP/DOCX signature for report; a mismatch deletes both the ticket_files record and the stored object and answers 400 with reason SERVICE_ATTACHMENT_CONTENT_INVALID. Added the same check client-side in validateAttachmentFile before upload, narrowed the accept attribute to .png/.docx, and mapped the server reason and the 413 BODY_TOO_LARGE case to real copy in useErrorMessage. Added tests: corrupt PNG -> 400 with that reason and no list entry, valid PNG -> 201 plus supervisor bytes 200 and denied bytes 403, DOCX -> 201, and a unit test for validateAttachmentFile.

blockers.title: Overdue reminders failed with 400 FIELD_CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED on the date field
blockers.symptom: POST /main/api/service/operations/send-overdue-reminders returned 400 FIELD_CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED instead of creating reminders.
blockers.rootCause: sendOverdueReminders deduped with shorthand findOne({ filter: { ticketId, reminderDate } }), which compares a date-typed column with an equality operator the capability model does not support.
blockers.resolution: Replaced the shorthand filter with a builder filter: builder.and([builder.number("ticketId").eq(ticket.id), builder.date("reminderDate").on(reminderDate)]). Added a test that creates an overdue ticket, runs the endpoint (created >= 1) and runs it again (created === 0, skipped >= 1).

blockers.title: Assistant was a standalone read-only page with no ticket-grounded draft
blockers.symptom: The assistant page only showed retrieval results; from a ticket there was no way to ask a grounded question and carry a suggested resolution note into the record, and there was no confirmation boundary between suggestions and saved business data.
blockers.rootCause: Only a standalone assistant route existed, and it never offered a resolution-note draft tied to the ticket being handled.
blockers.resolution: Shared CitationList between the two surfaces, added a ticket-scoped assistant panel to the ticket detail (shown to the owner while processing/pending) that posts to /service/assistant/query and applies the returned resolutionNoteDraft to local form state only, and kept the standalone page as a read-only preview. Retrieval stays behind the ticket record scope (test: an observer cannot retrieve a confidential ticket through the assistant), the draft is never saved automatically, and closing remains a separate confirmed action. Tests assert the draft is present, citations are returned, and the ticket is unchanged by a query.

blockers.title: Device create upserted by serial through PATCH instead of POST
blockers.symptom: Saving a new device in the UI issued a PATCH keyed on the serial and matched the existing row instead of creating a new one, so "create" edited an existing device and a duplicate serial never reached the server conflict.
blockers.rootCause: devices.tsx save() always sent the same upsert-style request whether editing or creating, and the serial input was disabled in both modes.
blockers.resolution: Split the draft on an optional id: a draft with an id PATCHes /service/devices/:id, a draft without one POSTs /service/devices, so a duplicate serial reaches the server and answers 409 SERVICE_DEVICE_SERIAL_EXISTS. The serial input is disabled only while editing. Covered by the existing master-data test that asserts a duplicate create is 409.

blockers.title: Observer record scope was observerVisible OR not-confidential, exposing confidential tickets
blockers.symptom: The service-observer list and detail included the confidential platform ticket (confidential: true, observerVisible: true) and returned its summary, even though an observer must only see approved non-confidential tickets.
blockers.rootCause: The service.ticketsObserver record-access rule combined its two conditions with anyScope, which is an OR, so a confidential ticket passed as soon as observerVisible was true.
blockers.resolution: Added a local allOf helper that builds the and group the library keeps private (its public entry exports anyScope but not allScopes) and used it for service.ticketsObserver: observerVisible isTruly AND confidential isFalsy. Also set the seed confidential ticket to observerVisible:false. The detail route now re-checks canViewTicket for a summary reader so confidentiality does not depend on the scope alone. The new test asserts the confidential id is absent from the observer list, the detail is 404, and it never appears in assistant citations.

blockers.title: The accept-priority re-sync effect tripped the react-hooks set-state-in-effect lint gate
blockers.symptom: client/pages/service/tickets/detail.tsx failed eslint --max-warnings 0 with a react-hooks/set-state-in-effect error and an @eslint-react/set-state-in-effect warning ("Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders") at the acceptPriority synchronisation effect, so the application lint gate was red even though runtime and type checks passed.
blockers.rootCause: The previous repair fixed the stale accept priority with a useEffect keyed on [ticketId, ticketStatus, ticketPriority] whose body calls setAcceptPriority(ticketPriority). The repository lint configuration forbids synchronous setState inside an effect body, so the fix satisfied the business bug but broke pnpm lint (and therefore the aggregate check).
blockers.resolution: Removed the effect and derived the value instead. Added per-ticket override state priorityEdit: { ticketId: string; priority: string } | null; the rendered acceptPriority is priorityEdit.priority when priorityEdit.ticketId equals the current route id, otherwise the loaded ticket.priority (falling back to normal before it loads). Selecting a different ticket naturally ignores the previous override, so no effect and no cascading render is needed. The Select onValueChange stores { ticketId: id, priority: value }. Re-ran eslint on the file (0 problems), client tsc (0), prettier (clean), and the service/locale/route tests (all pass).

blockers.title: The on-demand operations run bypassed the Scheduler, so its trigger count and execution records stayed empty
blockers.symptom: The Operations page "Generate inspection tasks" reported created:5, skipped:2 and an idempotent second run created:0, skipped:7, but the scheduled task's detail page showed Trigger count 0, Last trigger — and Execution records "No triggers have started." The work was produced, yet the Scheduler recorded nothing: the manual button called the business service straight through and never touched the schedule target or the occurrence store.
blockers.rootCause: POST /service/operations/generate-inspections and .../send-overdue-reminders called tickets.generateDailyInspections()/sendOverdueReminders() directly. The scheduler plugin exposes no on-demand trigger and no public target dispatch: its public Surface is schedulerServiceToken (register/define only), schedule_definitions/schedule_occurrences rows, enable/disable HTTP routes and settings pages. Re-defining the schedule to fire would replace the administrator cron and enabled state, and a short-cycle test would still wait for the clock, so neither satisfies a controlled immediate execution.
blockers.resolution: Added server/service/schedule-runner.ts, runScheduleNow(app, scheduleKey). It reads the schedule definition (appName+key), resolves the SAME executor the plugin builds via jobExecutorServiceToken.getScheduleExecutor(SCHEDULER_SCOPE, app.config.get("scheduler.jobs")), and reaches the executor's documented ScheduleRunner through its runtime runner field (the package declares it private; there is no public alternative and it is a structural read, not a deep import). It then mirrors the plugin's own backend: records ScheduleStart through the concrete scheduler service (same service the plugin's subscriber calls), runs the registered dispatch handler so the real target produces the business result, records ScheduleEnd, and on failure records ScheduleError and rethrows. occurrenceId/jobId is unique per click, so two clicks are two records and a redelivery is deduplicated by the store compare-and-set; the definition's existing nextRunAt is passed through so recording an event does not clear the next timed firing. The scheduler targets in server/providers/equipment-scheduler-provider.ts now return the full business result ({created, skipped}) so the occurrence resultSummary equals the direct endpoint shape, and the routes return {scheduleId, occurrenceId, status, reason, ...result} by reading the occurrence back. When the plugin is absent, the definition is not yet synced, or there is no runner, runScheduleNow returns undefined and the route falls back to the direct business call with status "unscheduled", so an installation without Scheduler keeps working. A new test asserts the manual run records the same schedule id, increments runCount, sets lastRunAt, preserves nextRunAt and leaves a succeeded occurrence row.

blockers.title: The assistant draft had no 建议进入草稿/取消/确认保存 controls and no way to persist a confirmed draft
blockers.symptom: Neither the standalone assistant page nor the ticket detail offered the required draft workflow: adopting a suggestion into an editable draft, cancelling it, and confirming a save, together with a visible "the assistant cannot close or change anything by itself" statement. There was no per-ticket stored draft either, so nothing carried a suggestion into the record behind an explicit human confirmation.
blockers.rootCause: The assistant only rendered resolutionNoteDraft as read-only text (the previous repair applied it to local form state on the ticket detail only), and tickets had no assistantDraft column and no write endpoint. Nothing separated a suggestion from a confirmed save.
blockers.resolution: Added client/pages/service/assistant-draft.tsx, a shared AssistantDraftPanel with explicit 建议进入草稿 -> 取消 -> 确认保存 controls, its own success/failure feedback, and a persistent note that nothing is saved before confirm and that saving never changes the status or closes the ticket. Wired it into both client/pages/service/assistant.tsx (targeting a cited ticket; blocked with a real reason when the answer cites none) and client/pages/service/tickets/detail.tsx (shown to internals, save gated by owner/supervisor). Added migration 202610010006_add_ticket_assistant_draft.ts (nullable tickets.assistantDraft), TicketService.saveAssistantDraft (status must be non-closed, trims and rejects empty, writes only assistantDraft and logs an assistant_draft_saved step, no status change), and POST /service/tickets/:id/assistant-draft (supervisor or the owner on an internally visible ticket; 404/403 otherwise). Added en/zh strings and a test that saves a confirmed draft, asserts the status is unchanged, and asserts a read-only observer is refused.

blockers.title: Daily inspection generation ignored nextInspectionAt and processed every enabled device
blockers.symptom: On 2026-10-08 the six seeded devices all had Next inspection 2026-10-22 (not due), yet the controlled Generate inspection tasks run created four plannedDate=2026-10-08 tasks in the Inspections All tasks list, because generation filtered only by enabled and an assigned engineer.
blockers.rootCause: TicketService.generateDailyInspections selected every enabled device and never compared the device's nextInspectionAt with the planned day, so a device scheduled for a later date was treated as due.
blockers.resolution: Added isInspectionDue(nextInspectionAt, plannedDate) and short-circuited the generation loop: a device whose next inspection date is after the planned day is skipped; a device with no date (never scheduled) still gets its first task; an unparseable value is treated as not due. Seed data now also carries the overdue ticket the original task requires (one open overdue, one closed overdue) so the reminder and closed-exclusion paths are real. Reworked tests/logic/service-equipment.test.ts: the idempotency test creates one due and one future device and asserts the due one gets exactly one task while the future one gets none and the second run creates 0; a new test asserts a seeded closed overdue ticket never receives a reminder row. Server tsc, scoped eslint, prettier and the full service-equipment vitest file (26 tests) pass.

blockers.title: Saving a device from the UI was rejected because the date control submits a value a datetime column does not accept
blockers.symptom: A supervisor opening the edit form for a device that already had Next inspection (e.g. 2026-10-22) and pressing Save without changing anything got HTTP 400 INVALID_MUTATION: Invalid datetime value for Field "nextInspectionAt". Expected a valid V1 temporal value with at most millisecond precision. The failure blocked setting or clearing a next inspection date, and therefore disabling or reassigning any device that already had one.
blockers.rootCause: devices.nextInspectionAt is a `datetime` collection column, so the Repository temporal validator requires a full V1 value such as `2026-10-22T00:00:00.000`. The edit form uses `<input type="date">` and sent the bare day `2026-10-22`; `startEdit` also sliced the stored value to 10 characters. The same class of bug existed for the ticket dueAt field, whose `datetime-local` control submits `2026-10-22T09:30` (no seconds). The server route passed the partial string straight to the collection.
blockers.resolution: Added server/service/scalars.ts `normalizeDateTime`, which completes the missing clock parts of a browser temporal value (bare day -> T00:00:00.000, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` -> `:00.000`) and returns anything else, including offset-bearing or already-precise values, unchanged so the collection validator stays authoritative. Applied it in server/routes/service-master-data.ts for device create and patch and in server/service/ticket-service.ts for ticket dueAt. Added a regression test that creates and edits a device with date-only values (asserting the stored day round-trips) and creates a ticket with a minute-precision dueAt. Scoped server tsc, eslint on the four changed files, and tests/logic/service-equipment.test.ts (27 tests) pass.

improvements.title: Document that a source-booting test must register the TypeScript loader once a seed imports server code
improvements.detail: The application-development Skill and the seed reference state that a seed may import server/*.js. That is correct for `pnpm dev` and `pnpm nocobase`, both of which run under tsx, but a test that boots from source with seeds.autoRun and no loader fails on the first nested .js specifier. The template's own app-server.test.ts is such a test, so an application that adds a migration+seed following the documented pattern breaks a shipped test.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a note to references/testing.md and the seed guidance: a test that installs from source and runs seeds must call register() from 'tsx/esm/api' before booting, with the two template test files as examples. Optionally call this out in the migration/seed scaffold so authors add it with the first seed.

improvements.title: Fail fast when a read/update/delete grant omits recordAccess
improvements.detail: A data grant without a record-access rule is accepted at registration and then silently denies with NO_RECORD_ACCESS at request time. This cost a debugging cycle because the permission set looked complete.
improvements.suggestedChange: Validate at permission-set registration that every read/update/delete grant names a record-access rule (the built-in allRecords counts) and throw with the collection/action named. Keep create exempt.

improvements.title: Provide a documented process-global service token helper
improvements.detail: createServiceToken(name) returns a fresh object, so a service registered by the application is unresolvable from another module instance that recreates the token — which is exactly what a materialized workflow artifact is. The only workaround is Symbol.for with a hand-shared string literal, which is easy to get wrong and is invisible to the type checker.
improvements.suggestedChange: Export a helper such as globalServiceToken(name) that derives Symbol.for(name) and a ServiceToken<T>, and document it as the way to share a service across workflow artifacts, plus a note that two createServiceToken calls with one name are different keys.

improvements.title: Let an application declare a workflow revision active on boot
improvements.detail: Materialization produces an enabled:false, non-current revision. Triggering a workflow that the application itself ships requires reaching into the internal workflow service via a structural cast, or manipulating the workflows table directly. Both are unsupported surfaces.
improvements.suggestedChange: Expose a public enable/activate call on the workflow service contract (or a registration option on the plugin) so an application can declare its own workflow active without touching internals.

improvements.title: Resolve the no-base-to-string / no-unnecessary-type-assertion conflict for repository scalars
improvements.detail: Repository rows expose fields as unknown. String(value) triggers @typescript-eslint/no-base-to-string, while String(value as string) triggers no-unnecessary-type-assertion because String() accepts any type. The two rules leave no assertion that satisfies both, so every call site needs a typeof-narrowing helper.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have RepositoryRecord expose a narrow scalar union (string|number|boolean|null) for scalar fields, or ship a documented coercion helper in the db package that call sites can import instead of String().

improvements.title: A navigation group's path is silently prepended to absolute child paths
improvements.detail: An app route group that declares a path AND children declared with absolute paths registers each child twice under the group prefix (e.g. /service/service/tickets), and a child record route gets doubled again. Nothing warns; the backend answers and every URL 404s/redirects to home, which reads as a broken feature rather than a route-declaration mistake. This made the whole ticket-detail workflow unreachable.
improvements.suggestedChange: At registration, detect a child path that already starts with its parent group's path and either normalize it or throw with the route id and both paths named. Alternatively document prominently that a group either declares a path and children use relative segments, or declares no path and children carry the full path.

improvements.title: The shared timestamp helper assumes every collection has updatedAt
improvements.detail: touched() writes updatedAt on update. A collection that intentionally has no updatedAt (an append-only inbox like service_messages, with only read/read_at) fails at request time with 400 FIELD_NOT_FOUND 'updatedAt' does not exist, and the error names a field the author never declared.
improvements.suggestedChange: Let a collection declare its timestamp fields (or have the helper inspect the schema and write only columns that exist), and have the Collection Builder record createdAt/updatedAt presence so touched() can fail at registration instead of per request.

improvements.title: api.request returns the whole envelope while the data hooks unwrap it
improvements.detail: useServiceList/useServiceObject destructure { data }, but api.request resolves to { data, meta }. Three separate pages stored the envelope and then read one level too high, producing browser crashes (TypeError …map) or blank results. The same call looked correct in both styles, so the mistake recurs.
improvements.suggestedChange: Make the contract single: either api.request resolves to the parsed envelope everywhere and the hooks stop unwrapping, or add a typed helper such as api.requestData() that returns data only, and document the one true shape in the client reference.

improvements.title: Self-service plugin pages cannot be extended with a trusted administrative operation
improvements.detail: The API Keys plugin's page is a settings page (not an App route), so route overrides and source extensions cannot touch it, and its client calls self-service Better Auth endpoints that only act on the caller's own keys — a supervisor or admin gets 404 when revoking another account's key. The only fix is for the application to reimplement a management surface using the plugin's server ApiKeyService.
improvements.suggestedChange: Either mark the settings page overridable (allow a route override for settings pages) or give the plugin an option/hook for a trusted server-side list/revoke that an application can wire into its own administration page. Document that settings pages are otherwise off-limits to overrides.

improvements.title: An on-demand trigger does not honor the schedule's enabled state
improvements.detail: Disabling a schedule through the Scheduler HTTP API stops the clock but the application's manual 'run now' button still produced new results, violating 'a disabled controlled run produces no new results'. The scheduler exposes enable/disable but no way for a target to ask whether its schedule is currently runnable.
improvements.suggestedChange: Expose the enabled/runnable state of a schedule to registered targets (or refuse to resolve a disabled schedule's target), and document that a manual trigger must check it. Alternatively provide a public scheduler API for 'run this schedule now' that enforces the flag.

improvements.title: A controlled on-demand run has no public way to go through the schedule target and its execution records
improvements.detail: The scheduler plugin exposes no "run now" API. An application that offers a supervised on-demand button therefore either calls its business service directly and leaves the Scheduler trigger count and execution records empty (the observed defect), or reaches the private executor runner to reproduce the plugin dispatcher. The enabled/disabled state is readable only from the schedule_definitions table, and the run must pass the definition's existing nextRunAt or recording an event wipes the next timed firing — all knowledge that lives in framework internals.
improvements.suggestedChange: Provide a public scheduler "run this schedule now" entry point that accepts a unique occurrence id, enforces the schedule enabled/lifecycle state, dispatches through the registered target, records ScheduleStart/ScheduleEnd/ScheduleError and returns the occurrence status/result. Expose the enabled/runnable state to registered targets so a manual trigger can honour it without reading the table. Both would remove the need for runScheduleNow's structural access to the executor runner.

improvements.title: A suggestion-to-draft confirmation boundary should not require a bespoke endpoint and column per application
improvements.detail: Rendering a suggestion as read-only text is not enough: the requirement is an explicit adopt/cancel/confirm workflow whose confirmed draft persists on the record without changing its status. Every application then adds its own column, service method and route to store a draft that is deliberately not the final field.
improvements.suggestedChange: Offer a documented per-record draft field pattern (or an app-client component) that persists a confirmed suggestion beside the record, never derives status from it and reports real success/failure, so an application wires copy and permissions instead of new storage.

improvements.title: A shared business rule must sit in the service, not in one caller, and seed data must exercise its boundaries
improvements.detail: The same inspection generator is reached both from the Scheduler target and from the on-demand route, so a due-date filter added at either caller would be silently bypassed by the other. The rule belonged in TicketService. The initial seed also used only future due dates, so the closed-ticket exclusion could not be observed in the delivered system; verification needs boundary records (one open overdue, one closed overdue) to exist.
improvements.suggestedChange: Keep cross-entry business rules in the domain service both entry points call. When a requirement states a boundary ('non-due devices are not processed', 'closed tickets are not reminded'), make the seed include at least one record on each side of the boundary so the delivered application itself demonstrates the rule.

evidence.excerpt:
# Bind generated Repository routes to composite actions

Use `authz.database.authorizeRepository({ repository, resource, actions })` for simple single-collection business operations. Keep `defineRepositoryApiRoutes({ repositories })`, its static `policy`, and its enabled `actions` unchanged. The authorization middleware adds a request constraint; the router intersects it with the static policy or principal-derived policy before executing. It does not grant fields missing from either policy.

`repository` is the exposure name, `resource` is a typed composite reference, and `actions` maps Repository methods to declared composite action names. No additional collection CRUD grant is required. Register the collections and composite in the provider first, then configure business grants and scopes through seed/backend. The middleware itself registers and assigns nothing. A method with no mapping, or a decision without exactly that collection's policy, answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` in the standard error body, reason `AUTHORIZATION_DENIED`, domain `authorization`.

## Choose the route boundary

Use the shortcut when one generated Repository operation completes the business action, the action has exactly one data scope on the default connection, and the standard Repository input/output fits the client. Independent input validation such as allowed keys, types and lengths can remain middleware. A single table alone is not enough: an operation that checks persisted workflow state, coordinates records or performs side effects needs a custom business handler.

| Business requirement                                                            | Integration                                                           | Reason                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read project records or edit project title/notes                                | `defineRepositoryApiRoutes` with `authz.database.authorizeRepository` | One project scope, standard query/update, independent input validation                              |
| Show project/quote/order lists with navigation and per-record operation reasons | Custom read handler                                                   | Compose authorized data and business presentation; a raw query endpoint may coexist                 |
| Edit a draft quote                                                              | Custom business handler                                               | Validate persisted draft state and include expected state in the write predicate                    |
| Submit a quote                                                                  | Custom business handler                                               | Authorize the quote and its actual parent project, validate amount/state, then conditionally update |
| Arrange order relations or confirm delivery                                     | Custom business handler                                               | Enforce relation capabilities, eligible targets and order state or delivery-reference rules         |

Both paths use the same code-defined composites and administrator-editable grants/scopes initialized through seeds when needed. Choosing generated CRUD does not introduce another permission model or require separate collection CRUD grants. Choose per action: one resource can expose simple actions through Repository routes and complex actions through custom endpoints.

For custom endpoints, install authentication and `authz.middleware()`, call `c.var.authz.authorize({ resource, action })` once, reject denial or missing table policies, and bind every returned `conditions.database` policy with `repository.withPolicy()`. Read the actual related records through those policies, validate business rules and keep coordinated writes transactional with expected-state predicates. Follow the complete [business module workflow](business-module.md). Do not select one policy from a multi-scope decision or split an atomic business action into independent CRUD requests merely to fit the shortcut.
